title: DEC-249 carrier: lore agents treats bytes matching any released skill template as out-of-date (not protected), generated hash list, reworded message, component ADR
description:
Found by quest-cli on 2026-10-31 while checking lore-cli#702 (0.14.2 bump), diagnosed read-only by the lore-cli worker. NOT release-blocking (leader, 2026-10-31); quest-cli regenerates its skill file on its side. DESIGN QUESTION for opum-doc, no code in this task until ruled.

SYMPTOM. After upgrading lore, an UNEDITED skill file generated by the previous release makes lore agents --check exit 6 with 'out-of-date-protected .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md' and the message 'bridge is out of date -- a hand-edited file needs lore agents --force to regenerate'. The message says hand-edited whether the file was hand-edited or is simply the prior release's own output.

MECHANISM. src/core/agent-bridge.ts planSkill (about lines 436-471): on-disk SKILL.md byte-equal to buildSkillDoc() is unchanged; differing is updated only under --force and not --check; otherwise protected (line 470, pending: desired). There is no other branch and no record of prior releases' generated bytes or hashes. The doc comment at lines 418-423 states the intent: a differing generated file may be a hand-edit and lore never silently clobbers it. The plain token is built at src/commands/agents.ts line 534.

EVIDENCE (scratch git repos, tags run via git archive, 2026-10-31). Generated with v0.14.1 then checked with the lore-cli#702 head dff81a03 (0.14.2): out-of-date-protected, exit 6; the only byte difference is one added line, the cache command (diff 69a70; pending exactly equals the file plus that line); agents --force exits 0. Generated with v0.13.0 then checked with v0.14.0: out-of-date-protected, so 0.14.0 shipped with the same behaviour. Generated with v0.12.0 checked with v0.13.0, and v0.11.0 checked with v0.12.0: up-to-date, because the template did not change in those releases. So the cause is any release that changes the skill template, not 0.14.2 specifically. v0.14.0 checked with v0.14.1 was also up-to-date.

FIX SHAPES (not chosen). A: keep a list of prior-release generated-skill hashes and classify a match as plain out-of-date, updatable without --force. Needs a maintained list per release and changes the --force contract. B: reword the protected message so it does not claim a hand edit (for example: differs from this lore's template; run lore agents --force to regenerate), with no behaviour change. Cheaper; leaves the exit-6-on-upgrade behaviour.
implementationNotes: RULING 2026-10-31 (opum-doc, DEC-249, option A), relayed verbatim by the leader: lore prior-template question ruled by opum-doc, not sent to the operator: A, recorded as DEC-249. Not in 0.14.2; the 0.14.2 status is noted. - Bytes that exactly match a template some released lore wrote are out-of-date, not protected. lore agents updates them without --force, and --check never calls them hand-edited. - The hash list is generated from released versions (tags, or recorded by the release run), never kept by hand. - Bytes matching no released template still need --force. The message drops the edit claim, in substance: "differs from every skill template lore has shipped (it may have been edited); review it, then run lore agents --force". - Why not B alone: telling every upgrader that an unedited file needs --force trains --force by habit, and that removes the protection for files that really were edited. - lore-cli carries it under its own task, in the next release that changes the template or sooner, and writes the component ADR naming DEC-249. STATUS: this task is the DEC-249 carrier. The diagnosis evidence is in the description. NOT in 0.14.2 and does not touch lore-cli#702. Implementation and the component ADR come under a later brief after 0.14.2 ships; the leader floor-checks them then (planSkill is src/core/agent-bridge.ts, so this is likely a runtime-behaviour change needing a CHANGELOG entry and tests).

DEC-249 (a1), from opum-doc, relayed by the leader 2026-10-31: no quest-side hand-edit guard now; if quest ever adds one, it takes DEC-249's shape. (DEC-249 itself, option A, is recorded in the note above; the leader's relay of it was received twice and was already recorded in lore-cli#705, a9ab1835.)
